title: Borderless window
description: The Fullscreen option gives a borderless popup window at 0,0 the size of the desktop (not topmost, the renderer always windowed) instead of Direct3D exclusive fullscreen; off keeps the old centred window with a title bar. Only in the world: login and character selection stay a framed 800x600 window (the client forces 800x600 there through Device::ForceDisplayResolution). The option's label and help are renamed to "Borderless Window" in the language dat (client-option-strings.json). Needs the code-space entry.

items.change: Fullscreen becomes a borderless desktop-sized window at 0,0, not topmost, with the renderer always windowed

edits.note: Device::LoadDisplayPreferences: a cave sets FullScreen = 0 and, when the option byte 0x818B68 is on and no resolution is forced (0x8381A0), the presentation size becomes GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXSCREEN, SM_CYSCREEN); the AllowFullScreenMode test is gone
Device::ChangePresentation: the window style comes from a cave: option on 0x92000000 (popup, visible), off 0x12CA0000 (as before)
ChangePresentation: the test that skips the frame metrics and the centring reads the option byte through a cave, so the window goes to 0,0
Device::Init: the windowed flag comes from the option byte (popup style, 0,0, no frame metrics when on)
Device::Init: the SetWindowPos always uses HWND_NOTOPMOST (neg al -> stc; nop)
cave: the LoadDisplayPreferences body and the style cave

items.change: The borderless window applies only in the world; login and character selection stay a framed 800x600 window

edits.note: Device::Init: the direct read of the option byte calls cave D
the style and frame-metrics caves call cave D instead of reading the option byte
the Device::Init cave calls cave D
cave D: ZF = (option off or the forced-resolution flag 0x8381A0 on)
